findings.title: Async legacy Create shares the request object and context with the storage write
findings.body: Create hands the same `obj` to Storage.Create and then to a goroutine calling Legacy.Create. Storage may mutate that object (e.g. set ResourceVersion, UID, or timestamps) while the goroutine reads it, which is a data race. The goroutine also uses `ctx` from the request; once the HTTP handler returns, the request context is cancelled, so the legacy write can fail or be cut short with the 10s timeout unrelated to the actual work. The legacy copy should get a deep copy of the object and a context detached from request cancellation (e.g. context.WithoutCancel).

findings.title: Async legacy Update reuses objInfo that storage has already consumed
findings.body: Update passes the same `objInfo` to Storage.Update and then to Legacy.Update in a goroutine. UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject is typically invoked with the stored old object and may mutate state or be non-reentrant; calling it again concurrently with the storage path is unsafe. The legacy update may also be computed from a different base object than the one storage used, so the two stores can diverge silently. The same request ctx is also reused after the handler returns.

findings.title: Delete records the object name as the kind label in metrics
findings.body: The storage duration metric on success is called with `name` in the kind position (`d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...)`), while every other call uses `options.Kind`. This pollutes the metric label cardinality with per-object names and breaks dashboards that group by kind.

findings.title: Storage failure in Update is recorded as a legacy failure
findings.body: When Storage.Update returns an error, the code calls recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration. The unified storage error is therefore counted against the legacy store and the storage metric is not updated, making both metrics wrong. Create's storage error path has the same mislabeling issue on the legacy side.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection duration recorded with the storage metric
findings.body: In the DeleteCollection goroutine the legacy result is reported via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...) rather than recordLegacyDuration. Legacy timings and errors are then mixed into the storage metrics.

findings.title: Delete attaches the base logger to the context, dropping the name and method fields
findings.body: Delete builds a scoped `log` with name, kind and method, but then calls `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`, so downstream logs from the storage/legacy calls lose the context fields that every other method in this file keeps.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget legacy writes have no way to surface failures or bound concurrency
findings.body: All mutating methods launch an unbounded goroutine per request for the legacy write, and failures are only logged as a metric (and the goroutine's log is not used). Under sustained write load goroutines and legacy writes can pile up without limit, and divergence between stores is only visible through metrics. At minimum a bounded worker or queue is needed, and the legacy error should be logged with the object identity.

findings.title: Mode 3 playlist tests assume legacy writes are synchronous
findings.body: In mode 3 the legacy write happens asynchronously, but doPlaylistTests checks the legacy /api/playlists list and per-item legacy GETs immediately after the k8s create/delete calls. These assertions will be flaky or fail whenever the goroutine has not finished, so the new mode 3 integration cases are unreliable. They need to poll/eventually-assert on the legacy side, or the test should check the legacy store only after waiting.

findings.title: No tests verify the legacy write happens or that legacy failures are ignored
findings.body: The mode 3 unit tests mock the legacy store with expectations but never assert they were called (no AssertExpectations), and the legacy goroutine may run after the test returns. There is no test that a legacy failure does not change the returned result, and none for the Create/DeleteCollection legacy paths. The core behaviour of mode 3 (sync storage, async legacy) is therefore not actually tested.

findings.title: Unrelated checksum entries added to go.work.sum
findings.body: The go.work.sum change adds many entries for unrelated modules (grafana-azure-sdk-go, prometheus-alertmanager, otel exporters, etc.) that this feature does not touch. This looks like an accidental tooling side effect and should be dropped from the PR or explained.
